data.bottom_line: Triggering an avalanche remains unlikely across the majority of terrain due to low snow coverage. Avalanche concerns are limited to steep, wind loaded, northerly high elevation terrain where recent snow sits above buried weak layers. Isolated pockets of instability exist, and cracking or collapsing within recent snow indicates unstable conditions. Stick to grassy, lower-angle terrain with deeper coverage, watch for signs of wind-loading, keep your margins wide until the snowpack fills in, and watch out for buried obstacles.
